# dsh-okf-guard

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that keeps agents on `kb.py` inside the OKF
knowledge base at `%USER

PROFILE%\knowledge`. The knowledge base's own git hooks
check every commit; this plugin stops the co

mmon mistakes earlier, before the
tool call runs, and tells the model the right command instead.
## What it does
**Blocks** (a DSH tool guard, so no other plugin or approval setting can allow it):

- `git add` and `git commit` in the knowledge base. Use `kb.py commit`.
- `--no-verify`, and changes

to `core.hooksPath`.
- Force-push, deleting remote branches (`--delete`, `--prune`, `:branch`), and

history rewrites (`rebase`, `filter-branch`, `filter-repo`, `update-ref`, `reflog expire`).
- `okf
index`, `okf validate --fix`, `okf lint --fix`, `okf fmt -w` on a folder, `okf new` and `okf init`.

- `okf mv`, `rm`, `merge` and `split` without `--no-index`, because they regenerate index files.
- W
riting, moving or deleting `log.md`, `.kb/`, `.githooks/`, `.git/` or `.gitattributes`, from a shell

command or a file tool. Copying them somewhere else is fine.
- Downloading or unpacking over them:
`-OutFile`, `curl -o`, `wget`, `tar -x`, `unzip`, `7z x` or `Expand-Archive` into those files or int

o a folder that holds them.
- Creating a new concept file by hand. Use `kb.py new`.
- Text that cont
ains the Windows account name or the user folder path, written into the knowledge base by a file too
l or a shell command. Names match as whole words. The name is worked out at run time and is never st
ored in this plugin.
**Asks the user first** (the normal DSH approval prompt):

- `git push`.
- Commands that throw away uncommitted edits: `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, `git
checkout` of files (`.`, a path, `--`, `-f`), `git switch --discard-changes` or `-f`, `git restore`

(except only unstaging with `--staged`), `git stash drop`, `git rm`.
- Commands that move commits:
`git reset` to another commit or `--soft`, `git pull --rebase`, `git branch -f` or `-D`, `git checko

ut -B`, `git switch -C`.
- Commands that make commits the pre-commit check never sees: `git cherry-p

ick`, `git revert`, `git am`, `git merge` (fast-forward-only merges and `--abort` are fine).
- `okf

mv`, `rm`, `merge` and `split` with `--no-index`.
- Downloading or unpacking into any other knowledg

rge` and `split` with `--no-index`.
- Downloading or unpacking into any other knowledge base folder.
When another plugin or hook also has a say, its deny or its own question wins over okf-guard's quest

## Set up a knowledge base (once)

Skip this if you already have one at `%USERPROFILE%\knowledge`. The plugin
guards a knowledge base;

it doesn't create one. To start a new one, you need
git with your name and email set, Python 3.8 or

later,
and the okf tool (`cargo install okf`). Then run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That creates `%USERPROFILE%\knowledge` from `template/`, with
`kb.py` (the tool agents use), the git

hooks that check every commit, and empty
indexes, and makes the first commit. It works the same on

macOS and Linux.
Give a folder to put it somewhere else (`npx -y github:John-UNOwen/dsh-okf-guard D:

\kb`),
and set `knowledgeRoot` to match (see Settings). It never touches a folder that
already has f

set `knowledgeRoot` to match (see Settings). It never touches a folder that
already has files in it.
Then try it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Replace every `TODO(kb)` line in the new file with real text, then commit it.
`kb.py commit` stages

the concept with its index and log lines, and the hook
checks the result:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

To keep the knowledge base on more than one PC, add a remote and push as usual.
On each other clone,

run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once, because git
doesn't copy that setting. If your Wind

ows account name could end up in paths
in some other form, add it with `git config kb.privateName "<

name>"`; the hooks
and this plugin both block it.
## Settings
Override them in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

`shellTools` (default `pwsh`, `bash`) and `fileTools` (default `write`,
`edit`, `str_replace_editor`
) name the tools whose calls are checked.
## Limits

- When a session's approval policy is "never" (the full-access preset), there
is nobody to ask, so t

he guard refuses instead of asking. Agents can't push
there; push yourself. The model sees the guard

's reason and a hint on how to
rewrite the command, not DSH's bare "the user rejected tool". A quest

ion
from another plugin or hook still shows up as DSH's rejection.
- It reads commands, it doesn't r

un them. A command that writes in an unusual
way (for example a `python -c` one-liner) can get past

it. The pre-commit
hook still checks everything at commit time.
- Variables set in the same command

are followed (`$repo = '...'`,
`Join-Path`, `"$repo\x"`, `"$($repo)\x"`, `$repo + '\x'`), also insid

e a block, and so are
environment variables, `$PWD`, loops and `ForEach-Object` over a literal
list

(`'a','b'`, `1..3`, or a variable holding one), checked once per value.
A variable set inside an `if

`, `try` or loop is unknown once the block ends,
one set in a function or script block is unknown fo

r the rest of the
command, and one set from a command's output is unknown. A write or a
knowledge ba

se git command that uses an unknown variable asks first, and so
does a splatted write (`Set-Content

@params`). Quoted literal paths never ask.
- It knows where a command runs from the session folder,

the shell tool's
`workdir`, `cd`, `cd -`, `pushd` and `popd` in the same command, `git -C`,
`--git-d

ir`, `--work-tree`, and `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE` set in the same
command.
- The 8.3 short form o

f the home folder (like `C:\Users\ABCDEF~1`) is looked
up in the background when the plugin starts,

so for the first moment short
paths are not yet recognized.
